findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed that the chemical dish machine was not sanitizing at an effective concentration of Chlorine (10ppm). CORRECTED: PIC determined that the sanitizer dispenser was empty and replaced the dispenser with a new bucket during the inspection. Chemical dish machine was then measured to be sanitizing at effective concentration of Chlorine for warewashing (50ppm). Ensure that chemical sanitizers used in mechanical warewashing are used per manufacturer’s instructions regarding pH.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
Observed the front dress prep cooler was not sufficiently cooling and cold holding TCS foods (see Violation #33):

(i) sliced tomatoes (probed 52°F) and shredded lettuce (47°F). CORRECTED: tomatoes and lettuce were voluntarily discarded, as they were prepared longer than 4 hours ago; previously prepped tomatoes and lettuce were taken from the walk-in cooler and placed in ice baths, which will be monitored for cold holding temperatures.

(ii) shredded cheese (52°F) and cooked spaghetti (56°F). CORRECTED: shredded cheese and cooked spaghetti were voluntarily discarded, as they were removed from proper cold holding temperatures longer than 4 hours ago; a new container of shredded cheese was prepared and new packages of cook spaghetti were moved from the walk-in cooler and both were kept in a nearby short cooler that was sufficiently cold holding.

(iii) milk (42°F) and manufactured sauces that require refrigeration (clucked sauce, mayonnaise, and garlic spread - 43°F). CORRECTED: sauces were moved to nearby coolers that were sufficiently cold holding.

Ensure that TCS foods are kept at temperatures of 41°F or less.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Observed the front dress prep cooler was not sufficiently cooling and cold holding TCS foods. PIC took care of TCS foods so that they will be properly cold holding in the interim (see Violation #22). PIC is contacting a repair company. Inspector will Follow Up with establishment to confirm that the prep cooler has been repaired. Ensure that equipment for cooling and cold holding is sufficient to provide food temperatures of 41°F or less.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment:
Observed that the following freezers had significant ice drip buildup that was falling onto food:
(i) the walk-in freezer. Staff had placed a pan to collect drips, but additional ice drips had formed missing the pan and falling onto food. CORRECTED: PIC moved food away from the fans where the ice is forming and dripping.
(ii) the 2-door standing freezer. CORRECTED: PIC placed a tray directly underneath where the ice drips are forming so that when they defrost they do not fall below onto the food.
Ensure that freezers do not get significant ice buildup, and that the ice does not contaminated the food stored in the freezers.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed there is an accumulation of grease and food reside underneath the burger grills. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of grease deposits and other soil accumulations. Ensure that underneath the burger grills is clean to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Observed the ice scoop at the drive through was stored with the handle in contact with the ice. Since the handle is touched by bare hands storing the scoop in this position poses the risk of contamination. The PIC and employee working the drive through were educated and the ice scoop was moved to another location. Ensure that scoops for ready-to-eat foods are always stored to prevent contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following must be cleaned:

(1) The food debris inside both of the microwaves on the prep line.

(2) The food debris on the shelf below the sauces on the prep line. 

(3) The dust on the hood system that is not in use anymore near the drive through and fryers. 

The above referenced were cleaned to sight and touch during the inspection. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The inspector educated the employee when the action was observed. Immediately afterwards the employee re-washed their hands using the proper procedure. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucet to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed that the following non-food contact surfaces required cleaning to protect food from cross contamination: (1) Inside the microwave located between the fryers and vegetable prep cooler; and (2) The fan blades in the walk-in cooler. The PIC cleaned both of these surfaces during the inspection. Ensure that food is protected from cross contamination during storage and preparation. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Observed knives and forks stored in a container adjacent to the vegetable prep cooler with handles and food-contact surfaces intermingled. Utensils must be stored with the food contact surfaces facing in the same direction to ensure only handles are touched by employees. The PIC removed the utensils, washed them in the dish machine, and stored the clean utensils in the correct storage order. Ensure that utensils are always stored correctly to protect them from contamination. 

4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed cleaning of the physical facilities to be actively occurring but incomplete at this time. Several areas with accumulation of debris still persist during the cleaning process. Inspector will perform a spot-check during previously scheduled follow-up on 08/25/2023. Continue to work on ensuring the physical facilities of the establishment remain clean to sight and touch and cleaning precludes the accumulation of residue and debris. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Inspector observed hand washing practices at the facility and observed the following:

-- Inspector observed an employee use improper procedure when washing hands. Employee was immediately stopped, instructed on proper handwashing procedure and the reason for the use of a barrier, and required to rewash hands properly. Inspector observed proper procedure used by this employee from that point forward. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Inspector observed hand washing practices at the facility and observed the following:

-- Hand washing frequency is inconsistent from one staff member to another. Obtain and post an SOP for handwashing either from the franchisor or develop a facility specific one, however, all staff must understand when hand washing is required.

-- The facility is short staffed and unable to manage hand washing with busy operations. Two employees and a manager were present on arrival. During this time, inspector observed an employee preparing food at the front grill with a slice of cheese in hand who then returned to the fryers, cheese still in hand, to turn off the alarm (using a glove hand to touch a soiled NFCS) on the fryer. Staffing must be sufficient to ensure that cross-contamination at the facility and two employees plus a manager is insufficient with any significant amount of business at the facility. The employee was immediately instructed to stay in one area, but this is not feasible with only two employees present. Failure to properly staff the store results in an inability to wash hands during appropriate intervals and the separation of activities required to prevent cross-contamination from occurring. Ensure that staffing is sufficient at all times to ensure food safety.

-- Inspector observed an employee return from cleaning activities to food preparation without hand washing between activities. Gloves are NOT a replacement for proper hand washing. When switching activities that result in the potential contamination of the hands, such as cleaning the dining room, gloves must be removed, hands must be washed, and new gloves must be donned before working with food. Ensure that staff is aware that any activities in the dining room such as cleaning, picking up consumer trays, and so forth must be followed by hand washing due to potential contamination from consumers visiting the facility.

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Person-in-charge (PIC) has several repeat and/or priority/priority foundation violations during the inspection today. 

PIC advised inspector that the majority of accumulation had occurred prior to her appointment as CFM at the facility which is correct. This violation was observed during the previous inspection and corrective actions were required as of today's date. Further, PIC advised inspector that a list of all areas requiring cleaning was not itemized in the previous report. As noted in the previous report, cleaning is required underneath ALL pieces of equipment in the facility. The PIC must be able to identify areas which do not comply with 2017 FDA Food Code as part of the responsibilities of a CFM. The responsibility for identifying all areas of the facility which require cleaning does not fall on SCDPH but on the facility.

Due to the priority/priority foundation and repeat violations observed during the inspection today, a 30-day follow-up is issued to evaluate the overall state of compliance at the facility. Ensure that no priority or priority foundation violations exist in the facility at that time. Inspector will return on 08/25/2023.

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM 08/25/2022.

Inspector did not observe any hand washing occurring during the inspection today. Inspector put a crease in the corner of the paper towel roll at the front hand sink after washing hands at the start of the inspection. The crease was still present in the paper towel roll at the end of the inspection indicating that hand washing had not occurred at that sink. Inspector did not observe any hand washing at the back hand washing sink. Several glove changes occurred without hand washing between glove changes. Inspector observed an employee go from taking orders and accepting payment to working with food without hand washing, although gloves were changed between activities. Ensure that hand washing is occurring immediately before working with food AND any activites which may have contaminated employee's hands. A follow-up is issued for 07/28/2023 to observe hand washing practices within the facility at that time.

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Inspector did not observe any sanitizer buckets made during the inspection. At the end of the inspection, staff was asked whether any sanitizer buckets were made at that time. Staff looked around for sanitizer buckets but did not find any. Two sanitizer buckets were made to proper concentration at that time. Corrected on site. Ensure that staff are aware that sanitizer buckets must be available at ALL times of operation when food preparation is occurring.

4-703.11: After cleaning, FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be SANITIZED in: (A) manual hot water operations. (B) mechanical hot water operations. (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use  standard contact time 30 seconds.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Foods in the prep cooler along the south wall of the kitchen where sandwiches are made was observed to have temperatures around 50 to 55 degrees F. Temperatures in the prep cooler must be maintained at 41 degrees or below. The facility does not have a time-as-a-control policy which states that items in the cooler are discarded after 4-hours in the prep cooler. The lid to the prep cooler was left open on inspector arrival allowing foods to warm to within the critical range above 41 degrees. Inspector closed the lid during the inspection. Ensure that staff are aware to keep the lid to the cooler closed. If the lid is to remain open and foods are observed to be out-of-temperature, establish a time-as-control policy and discard all TCS foods in the prep cooler at the end of 4-hours. Ensure that ALL TCS foods not covered under a time-as-control policy are kept at 41 degrees or below at all times. A follow-up is issued for 07/28/2023 to ensure cold-holding temperatures in the prep cooler are below 41 degrees and/or establish time-as-control policy.

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Three pieces of equipment within the facility appear to be in disrepair. 
- The microwave oven in the kitchen above the steam table has a broken handle. The handle must be repaired/replaced.
- The ice machine is leaking along pipes behind it resulting in standing water and mold growth on pipes, floor and equipment. The ice machine/plumbing must be repaired/replaced.
- The hot-water heater is in the process of being replaced but there is standing water underneath it. The new hot water heating is present and pending contractor availability for replacement. Ensure that this repair is finished by the next routine inspection.

All repairs/replacements must be completed by the next routine inspection in 2023. 

4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.comment:
Drainage from the ice machine is observed to be pooling on the floor underneath and behind the ice machine. Ensure that this water is drained appropriately and the areas subject to water are cleaned and sanitized to remove/prevent mold growth. 

5-403.12: Condensate drainage and other non-SEWAGE liquids and rainwater shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to LAW.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM PREVIOUS INSPECTION DATED 03/21/2023.

Inspector observed the floors underneath all pieces of equipment in the kitchen to be soiled with grease, refuse and debris. The majority of the accumulation observed during the inspection today was also observed during the inspection on 03/21/2023 prior to the current CFM taking over as person-in-charge (PIC). 

Heavily soiled areas include but are not limited to underneath and behind the cash register counter, the reach-in coolers to the left of the grill, the grill, the steam table, the corner counter reaching to the drive thru, the counter to the right of the drive thru, the fryers, and the prep cooler to the right of the fryers, the double upright fry freezer to the left of the fryers, and the dish machine. Underneath/beneath each of these items (and any others within the kitchen itself not explicitly listed) is large accumulation of soil that has been present since prior to the previous inspection. These areas are required by 2017 FDA Food Code as adopted by the State of Illinois to be clean often enough to prevent such accumulation from occurring. 

The severity of the soil accumulation is of serious concern for the harborage of pests in the future as well as the growth and spread of pathogens as the accumulation worsens. PIC has stated concerns with being able to move the equipment to clean. Food code requires that equipment be constructed in a manner which allows it to be easily cleanable.

A follow-up is issued for 08/04/2023 to allow time for cleaning to occur. Ensure that corrective actions have been taken to bring the facility back into compliance by this date. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
Person-in-charge (PIC) has not completed allergen awareness training as required by this statute. Ensure that allergen awareness training is completed by the PIC by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The hand sink near the dish area of the kitchen has caulking along the back which is molded and deteriorating. Re-caulk the sink to create a surface which is smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. Ensure that all surfaces subject to food/moisture are smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. This is a repeat violation from the previous inspection. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed there to be a large amount of residue, debris and refuse underneath counters and equipment throughout the kitchen especially underneath the grill. Ensure that all areas of the facility, even those which are hard to reach, are cleaned often enough to prevent the accumulation of residue and debris. Ensure that all areas underneath counters and equipment are clean by the next routine inspection. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a large spatula used for stirring the spaghetti which was stored on a shelf visibly soiled with dust. Cleaned and sanitized utensils must be stored in a location which is cleaned and sanitized to prevent contamination of foods prepared using the utensil in question. Ensure that utensils are stored in clean and dry locations that are protected from cross contamination.

4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The hood and wall behind where the buns are stored is visibly soiled with ketchup splatter which has been sitting long enough to allow it to dry. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces of equipment and walls are cleaned regularly and when soiled. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed that the following areas of the facility must be re-caulked:
- The hand sink in the back of the facility has caulking which has begun to deteriorate.
- The prep sink has caulking which has molded and is deteriorating.
- The piece of sheet metal behind the spaghetti pot has peeling and deteriorating caulk.
- The areas to the right of the dish machine which junction with the sheet metal behind the counter are missing most areas of caulking and are not sealed to the wall. 

Surfaces which are subject to moisture must be smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. Areas which have missing/molded/deteriorated caulking are not smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable and must be re-caulked. Ensure that these are caulked by the next routine inspection. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed operators working with meat, cups, utensils, bags and other materials proceed to switch gloves and work with RTE food without hand washing in between activities. Ensure that anyone handling food washes hands between activities and glove switching to prevent cross contamination. Discussed with PIC who states understanding and employees have been corrected. Observed employees washing hands appropriately during inspection. Corrected on site. 

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Frozen condensation was observed leaking from both the upright freezer and walk-in freezer onto food packaged in non-waterproof packaging. Containers have been moved and a tray placed underneath the condenser to protect food. Ensure that freezers are monitored for signs of frozen condensation and protect food accordingly. Corrected on site.

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
The mop room floor is heavily soiled and wet. Upon entry into the room, inspector observed several flies present in the room. On further inspection, inspector observed the flies were coming from large black equipment in the middle of the room with a dirty mop head and from behind the equipment in the room which had a large amount of debris and residue. Conditions such as these harbor and promote pest problems in the facility. Ensure the room is cleaned and stays dry and eliminate the flies from the facility. Contact pest control if internal measures are insufficient to prevent pest problems. 

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Several wiping cloths were observed throughout the facility including but not limited to sitting next to the meat station, under the hand sink, and near the prep cooler. Dry cloths may be used to handle hot handles on cooking equipment/utensils. Wet cloths must be stored in sanitizer solution to prevent the growth of contaminants in the rags. 

4-901.12: Wiping cloths laundered in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT without mechanical dryer shall be air-dried in location and manner that prevents contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES. Wiping cloths may be stored in sanitizer solution after laundering.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
Single use forks at the drive through are observed to be facing handles towards the rear which requires employees to grab forks by the eating surface instead of the handles. Ensure that all single use and reusable utensils are stored and displayed with handles facing out to ensure that employees can grab the handles without contaminating the eating surfaces of these utensils. 

4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed a cooler to the left of the grill that has broken clips and a shelf which is falling over. PIC states maintenance has been notified. The shelf is touching water lines and is in need of cleaning. Ensure that the shelf is repaired by next inspection to prevent contamination and facilitate easy cleaning. 

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
A personal phone was sitting on the counter at the front of the restaurant next to the hand sink. Personal phones should be stored away from cooking/prep areas. The phone has been moved from the area and employees have been advised to keep personal items separated from food handling areas. 

6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

At the time of the inspection, no one in the facility could provide a CFPM certification. Per the PIC, two of the employees are scheduled to take the class in the near future but have not at this time. PIC is instructed to ensure that a CFPM is on site at all times the facility is in operation.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Multiple employees are observed during the inspection to improperly wash hands. Employees were observed to wash hands, turn off the faucet with their bare hands and then pick up paper towels to dry their hands. Inspector discussed with the PIC ands they are instructed to review with ALL employees proper hand washing procedures.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Cooked pasta in the prep cooler next to the steam table is observed with internal temperatures of 50F-55F. Per discussion with the PIC, the items were removed from the walk cooler approximately an hour before observation and were moved back to coolers to bring back into temperature control during the inspection. The cooked past will now be stored in the reach in cooler under the prep cooler from now on per the PIC.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

The scoop used for ice in the drive thru area was observed stored in the ice with the handle in contact with the ice. There is a pan next to the ice bin specifically for the scoop. PIC was notified and the employee responsible for the area educated. The scoop was moved during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text: 2-201.11 Reporting Agreements not available for employee illnesses. situation discussed with the PIC and hand outs/ examples given. Follow up in 2 weeks

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16 The mix used for whipped cream is observed with internal temperatures between 43-45F. Package indicated cold holding is required, therefore it should remain at 41F or less at all times. The machine was taken out of service until a time where the mix can be maintained at safe temperatures. Follow up Tuesday.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

At the time of the inspection, no one in the facility could provide a CFPM certification. Per the PIC, two of the employees are scheduled to take the class in the near future but have not at this time. PIC is instructed to ensure that a CFPM is on site at all times the facility is in operation.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

The hand sink by the grill is observed without paper towels. Paper towels were supplied during the inspection to correct. PICs are instructed to ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The dish machine is not registering sanitizer on either the inspector of facility test strips. An error message is also observed on the display screen. PIC is instructed to contact EcoLab for service. The three part sink is being filled with sanitizer to complete the sanitize step until maintenance can be completed. Inspector will follow up Monday for compliance.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Cooked pasta in the prep cooler next to the steam table is observed with internal temperatures of 55F-61F. Per discussion with the PIC, the items were removed form the walk in approximately an hour before observation. Items will be discarded after 4 hours (8 pm). The pans being used for them in this cooler are shallow and the PIC believes that deeper pans will remedy the situation for the future. They are instructed to ensure that the TCS foods are maintained in proper temperature ranges at all times.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

1) A visibly soiled spatula is observed stored in the gap between the grill and the adjacent steam table. A discussion took place with the PICs and the spatula moved to dish for cleaning. 2) Dixie cup are being used for scooping salsa and onion at the sandwich prep station. Any ready to eat  (RTE) food should be dispensed using a scoop with a handle. The cups were removed during the inspection.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment: 3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. A knife was observed stored in the gap between the food containers and the wall of the prep cooler. This space is not easily cleanable. PIC is instructed to ensure that in use utensils are stored so as to prevent contamination of the working surfaces. The knife was replaced and moved to dish to correct.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment: 4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. A container of lids used for shake toppings/ ingredients is observed with the bottom soiled with food debris and sauce splash. Multiple lids appear to have made contact with these contaminates as well. PIC is instructed to ensure that cleaned items used for food storage are maintained clean in the facility. The tub in question was moved to dish for cleaning to correct.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: 6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. The baffles for the hood system have been removed for cleaning. This leaves the exposed grease build up in the vent exposed above the foods and utensils used for the fryers. PIC is instructed to place the baffles back prior to service resuming in the future.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: Observed handwashing sink without paper towels. Ensure handwashing stations have all necessary items readily available for use. Corrected. Towels replaced. Reference 6-301.11

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment: Observed seal on freezer in bad repair. Ensure all food and non-food contact surfaces are in good repair. Fix seal. Reference 4-501.11.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment: Observed employee put gloves on hand without washing hands in-between. Corrected. Education regarding handwashing has been provided. Handwashing will occur before any glove use and between tasks. Reference 2-301.14.

findings.comment: Repeat #1: Observed food equipment setting in soiled metal containers. Ensure food equipment is cleaned and placed in cleaned location. Corrected. PIC will clean soiled food-contact surfaces. Ensure all food contact surfaces are cleaned with proper frequency. Reference 4-601.11(A).

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment: Observed two ice scoop handles to be touching ice. Ensure ice scoop handles are placed in manner to prevent any potential contamination from occurring. In addition, ensure single-use items are stored appropriately. Reference 3-304.12.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed top of microwave soiled with debris. Observed R-I Freezer #1 and #2 (located near fryers) to be soiled. Observed ice cream cooler to be soiled. Ensure non-food contact surfaces are cleaned as needed to prevent accumulation. Clean areas. Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: REPEAT #2: Observed areas under equipment to be soiled with debris. This includes areas under fryers, under cold holding units, under tables, and under dry storage racks. Ensure food debris is removed in timely manner. General cleaning must be implemented and maintained to ensure areas remain clean. Reference 6-501.12 (A & B).

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored

Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed multiple food products being stored in unlabled white bags. 
Observed multiple unlabled containers with unidentifiable products.
All unlabled products must be either unmistakable or labled with proper labeling. 
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed several items out of temperature. Time-temperature abuse is occuring with several products. These include cut leafy greens and cut tomatoes. Products are discarded. 

750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed refrigeration adjacent to ice cream work station. These included milk-based product and cut leafy greens. Temperatures were probed at 47F with unknown amount of time out of temperature. Products were discarded. 

750-140 All refrigeration units used to store potentially hazardous foods shall be able to maintain proper product temperature at 41°F or below.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
1) Observed opened plastic bag inside food product. No physical debris can be placed inside food product during storage.
2) Observed  multiple foods being dispensed with cups. Facility must use proper dispensing utensils to prevent contamination. 
750-160(a) Food shall be prepared with the least possible manual contact, using suitable utensils and using surfaces that have been cleaned, rinsed, and sanitized to prevent cross-contamination.
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed frost build up in walk in freezer. Frost build up was observed on and above food storage. All food must be protected from potential contamination. 
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed ventilation above fryers to be soiled. All non-food contact surfaces must be clean. Clean as needed. 
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment:
Observed various personal items being stored near food storage areas. All personal items must be segregated from food prep and food storage areas. 
750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
Only one FSSMC was verified. FSSMCs must be present for all times of operation for category I operations. 

750-540 All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager.
